name: Mugain

attributes.attribute: a heroine who was the sister of Medb of Connaught
mother of Aed Slane, a hero and king
burned with envy over a gold headdress and was shamed
forced to bear a lamb and a salmon before a child

sources: MacNeill, Máire. The Festival of Lughnasa, Parts I and II. Dublin: Comhairle Bhéaloideas Éireann, 1982, 326-327.
Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Mugain is an Irish heroine in the old tales. She was a sister of the great queen Medb of Connaught. In the story she became the mother of Aed Slane, a hero and king. But before that birth she had to learn to treat other women well. She was a co-wife of the king of the high plain of Tara, sharing him with a woman named Mairenn. Mugain burned with envy over a fine gold headdress that Mairenn always wore. Suspecting her rival hid something, Mugain paid a member of the court to pull it down and shame her. The plan fell back on her. The moment the headdress fell, fine gold hair lay plain on Mairenn's head. Mugain was made to give birth to a lamb, and then to a salmon, before she could bear a human child. Some books join her with the goddess who ruled the south of Ireland.
